spec_source.note: This checked-in JSON file is the canonical contract source for v0.6.0; .rct planning files are not required inputs for this release gate. v0.6.0 is v0.5.0 plus #/mob_addressing: nothing of v0.5.0 is removed or changed for a request that names no mob.

mob_addressing.note: A Console of a gateway that hosts more than one mob. A request names the mob it is for; a request that names none is for the launch mob (the mob the gateway's launch names) and is served the bytes of contract v0.5.0. Nothing here adds a method or a route. Two refusal kinds are added, both of the naming of a member (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id/refusals).

capability.name: mob_addressing
capability.client_rule: A client sends mob_id or mobs only to a gateway that lists the name. A gateway that does not list it ignores mob_id on most methods and answers for its one mob, so a client that sent it would be answered for the wrong mob without an error.
capability.one_mob: The name says that the gateway judges mob_id and mobs, not that it hosts more than one mob. A console that serves one mob alone lists it too: it serves that mob for a request that names no mob and for one that names the mob's own id, and it refuses a request of this contract that names any other id, for every caller. The mobs a host has are the ones the experience lists (#/mob_addressing/listed_mob).
capability.vocabulary: feature_capabilities is an open list (tolerant: a reader ignores a name it does not know). The name mob_addressing is exact.
capability.member_mob_id: A gateway that lists mob_addressing also reads member_mob_id (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id) and writes member_mob_id and member_name on its member rows. A client sends member_mob_id to no gateway that does not list the name: such a gateway would read the member word alone.

mob_id.name: mob_id
mob_id.value: A mob id as topology.live_snapshot.mobs[].mob_id lists it.

params_member.rule: A top-level member of the request's params, on every meta/* method. It is read once and taken off the params before the method reads them; meta/mob_events/query keeps it as its own parameter too.

mob_id.launch_mob: No mob_id, null (in a body or in params), or the launch mob's own id: the request is served as one that names no mob.
mob_id.judged: The id is judged once, with the caller, right after the door knows its caller (401 comes first) and before any rule of the method or route. A caller may address a mob other than the launch mob when access control is not enforced, when the caller is an administrator, or when an allow rule that applies to the caller lists the mob in mobs. Every caller the Console lets in addresses the launch mob.

refusal.rule: The one answer of a door for an id it does not serve to its caller, whatever the reason and whoever asks: equal in status, headers and body. It names the requested id and no other mob. A refused request loads no mob.
refusal.vocabulary: closed: this contract has one refusal of a mob id. A second kind would be a breaking change.

not_a_string.rule: A mob_id in a body or in params that is neither a string nor null.

mobs_selector.name: mobs
mobs_selector.meaning: Every mob this caller may address: the launch mob and each other mob the gateway hosts that the caller may address (#/mob_addressing/mob_id/judged). It is the word the access rules use for every mob.
mobs_selector.placement: A query parameter on the routes, a top-level member of params on the methods. The POST routes take no selector: a mobs query parameter on them is refused, and a member mobs in their JSON body is not the selector.

valid_on.condition: GET /console/timeline and meta/console/query_timeline take it only on a request without identity.

mobs_selector.without_it: Each of the three reads answers for the launch mob alone, as in contract v0.5.0; a member row and a topology node also carry the members this contract adds (#/mob_addressing/row_key/row_members).

when: mobs together with identity on GET /console/timeline or meta/console/query_timeline
mobs on any other route or method

mobs_selector.loads_nothing: A read with mobs=* loads no mob and is no use of a mob: a mob that is not loaded stays not loaded. A periodic read never keeps a mob loaded. A timeline read with mobs=* answers no frame of a mob that is not loaded, and its cursor moves past that mob's stored frames.
mobs_selector.judged_per_entry: Each listed mob, each member row and each frame is judged for the caller in its own mob. A mob the caller may not address contributes no entry, no row, no frame and no count.
mobs_selector.vocabulary: closed: * is the one value. A gateway refuses every other value, so a later value is a breaking change for a client that sends it to a gateway of this contract.
mobs_selector.host_lists: The lists of the host that name members take mobs=* in params: meta/gating/pending, meta/gating/audit, meta/gating/questions, meta/console/attention and the console audit read meta/console/audit. Without it a list answers, of the entries members made, those of the launch mob's members alone: the bytes of contract v0.5.0 for those entries, so a client that does not ask for every mob is served no entry of another mob's member. A request made with no origin is no member's entry: with mobs=* and without it, meta/gating/pending and meta/gating/audit serve it to the callers who may address the mob it was made for, as a request of the mob that stands under that mob's id. With mobs=* it answers the entries of every mob the caller may address, each entry judged for the caller in its own mob and each entry a member made naming its mob (#/mob_addressing/row_key/host_list_entries). The list stays one list of the host either way: mob_id selects nothing on it. meta/decisions/list is not among them: a decision row names no member and no mob.

scopes.note: Every RPC method and route of this contract names its scope in mob_scope. The words are this document's, not the wire's.
scopes.host: The method answers from values of the host and never takes a mob as a selector of what it answers. A mob_id on it is judged like any other (a mob not served to the caller is refused) and selects nothing. Its lists are one list for a person: each entry is judged for the caller in the mob the entry was recorded for.
scopes.one_mob: The method is served for the mob the request names and reads only that mob's values. The request doors serve a mob other than the launch mob on the methods of this scope and on no other method of this contract. They serve further methods that this contract does not list, some of them for the mob a request names.
scopes.launch_mob_only: The door answers from wiring that is the launch mob's alone: a request on it that names any other mob is answered #/mob_addressing/mob_id/refusal for every caller, an administrator included. A door leaves this scope when its reads are per mob: a request that was refused is then served, which is an addition. In this version a member's own stream (GET /console/identity/{identity}/stream, and GET /console/timeline/stream or GET /console/timeline with mob_id) and the three /console/mcp-apps/* routes are launch_mob_only: a request on one of them that names another mob is answered #/mob_addressing/mob_id/refusal. The frames of a member of another mob are read from the one stream with mobs=* and from meta/console/query_timeline naming mob_id and identity. A method of this contract of this scope is one whose reads are not per mob in this version (#/mob_addressing/limits/methods).

launch_mob_only_methods.note: Methods of the request doors that are not part of this contract's method list and are launch_mob_only.

scopes.methods_outside_this_contract: The request doors serve further meta/* methods that this contract does not list, some of them for the mob a request names. No Console of this contract sends them, and this contract says nothing of them.

listing.without_mobs: The launch mob and the mobs nested under it. Contract v0.5.0 states no list of mobs: the list is this contract's. A mob the gateway hosts beside the launch mob is not in this list and none of its members is a row of this document.
listing.with_mobs: With mobs=*: also every other mob the gateway hosts that the caller may address, loaded or not, each at the top level, and the mobs nested under each.
listing.one_door: A hosted mob is listed once and served by its own door only: its members are reached by no request that names no mob.
listing.counts: Every count of the document counts what the document lists to the caller.

fields.mob_id: The mob's id. Unique on a gateway.
fields.parent_mob_id: The nearest listed mob it is nested under. Absent for a top-level mob.
fields.host_identity: The row key of the member that created it, while that member is listed to the caller.
fields.member_count: How many of the mob's members the document lists to the caller. Absent for a mob that is not loaded: nothing is counted for it.
fields.default: true for the launch mob. Absent or false for every other mob.
fields.incarnation: An opaque token of this creation of the mob. A reader compares two values of one mob_id for equality and reads nothing else from it: when it differs from the value the reader last saw for that id, the mob was created again and the reader drops everything it kept under the id.

meaning.stopped: The mob does not run: stopped, completed or failed.
meaning.dormant: The mob is known and not loaded. It has no member rows and no member_count. A request that names it loads it.
meaning.unavailable: The mob's store did not load. It is not loaded: it has no member rows and no member_count.
meaning.unknown: Nothing observed, or a value the reader does not know.

state_values.vocabulary: tolerant: a reader reads a value it does not know as unknown. A later value is not a breaking change.

meaning.host: The gateway's host created the mob. It is a top-level mob with a door of its own.
meaning.member: A member created the mob. It is nested under that member's mob and reached through the door of the mob at the top of its tree.

provenance_values.vocabulary: tolerant: an open list. A reader places a mob by parent_mob_id whatever the word, and takes a mob's door from default and the word host alone (#/mob_addressing/row_key/door).

row_key.note: How a member row is keyed in the document and how a request addresses the member. Shared cases: crates/meerkat-meta/src/console_row_key_cases.json.
row_key.row_key: A member row is keyed by the door it was read on. On the launch mob's door the key is the member's name as that door knows it: the bare name for a member of the launch mob (the bytes of contract v0.5.0), <nested mob id>/<name> for a member of a mob nested under it. On the door of another hosted mob the key is <the door's mob id>/<the member's name as that door knows it>. The key is presentation and a reader's own key. What is unique across the gateway is the mob a member sits in and its name there (member_mob_id and member_name of its row); two members of one door can spell one key (#/mob_addressing/row_key/shared_spelling).
row_key.member_rows: agent_sidebar.live_snapshot.agents[]: identity is the row key. mob_id names the door the row was read on (the launch mob's id on the launch mob's door) and never the member's own mob. member_mob_id names the mob the member sits in and member_name its bare name there: a reader takes a member's own mob and its name from these two, never from the key. The three say the same on every read of the experience, with the selector and without. A topology node (topology.live_snapshot.nodes[]) is read on its own door and names its member as a frame does: identity is the name as that door knows it, mob_id the door, and it carries member_mob_id and member_name as a row does; the read over every mob lists no node of another hosted mob.
row_key.door: The door of a member is the mob its row names in mob_id: the mob at the top of its mob's tree (by parent_mob_id) when that is a hosted mob other than the launch mob (provenance host, default not true), else the launch mob. A request for the member carries mob_id = the door's id, absent for the launch mob's door, and names the member either by member_mob_id and its bare name (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id) or by the one string that door knows it by: the bare name for a member of the door's own mob, <nested mob id>/<name> for a member of a mob nested under it. A mob id never holds '/'; a member's name may. An identity given as one string splits at its first '/', and its first part names a mob only when that mob is listed under the same door; else the whole string is a name of the door's own mob.
row_key.row_names: Every name a member row carries of its own member is the row key: identity, member_id and agent_id are equal, and a label agent_identity, where the row carries one, equals them: a reader may key a row by any of the three. The member's bare name stands in member_name alone. Names of other members inside a row (wired_to, side_chat_of) are row keys too.
row_key.host_list_entries: An entry of a list of the host that names a member names it by the pair of a frame (#/mob_addressing/frame): mob_id, absent for the launch mob's door, beside the member's name as that door knows it, in the same object. Pending gating entries, gating audit records and question sets carry the pair in origin (origin.mob_id, origin.identity); attention entries and console audit rows carry mob_id beside the name they already carry. A question set is a launch mob member's alone in this version (a member of another mob is answered that no person can be asked), so its origin carries no mob_id. A reader finds the entry's row with the frame rule and never by the bare name alone. An entry of a member of another mob than the launch mob is served only to a request that asked for every mob (#/mob_addressing/mobs_selector/host_lists). A decision row (meta/decisions/list) names no member and no mob.
row_key.launch_mob_by_id: A pair that names the launch mob by its own id is the launch mob's pair: a request, a frame or an entry of a host list whose mob_id is the launch mob's id is read as one without mob_id. Such a frame and such an entry are served to a request that did not ask for every mob.

row_members.vocabulary: tolerant: the three are optional members of a row. A gateway that does not list mob_addressing writes none of them; a reader then reads the row as a row of the launch mob's door, as in contract v0.5.0.

row_key.shared_spelling: Two members of one door can spell one key: a member of the door's own mob whose name has the form <nested mob id>/<name>, and the member <name> of that nested mob. The two differ in member_mob_id and member_name alone, and no reading of the one string tells them apart. In this version neither of the two has a member row on a console that lists the members of nested mobs (#/mob_addressing/limits/shared_spelling_rows). A request that names such a spelling by one string is answered by the members its method would answer the caller for: where the method would answer for both, a method that takes member_mob_id and reads the name from identity (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id/methods) refuses the request, and each is addressed by member_mob_id and its bare name; every other method reads the request for the member of the door's own mob, and such a caller cannot name the nested member on it; where for one, that one is served as if the other did not exist; where for neither, the request is answered as for a member the mob does not have. An ended member whose records the caller may still read counts for a method that reads; for a method that acts only live members count. The refusal is #/mob_addressing/member_mob_id/refusals.

frame.rule: A served frame names the door it was recorded by: mob_id is the door's mob, absent for the launch mob's door (such a frame is the bytes of contract v0.5.0), and identity is the member's name as that door knows it. The two are the two parts of the member's row key: identity alone on the launch mob's door, <mob_id>/<identity> on another door. A reader files a frame by them and reads nothing of the list of mobs for it; a frame of a door the list does not hold belongs to no row. The one-string pair of a request is the pair of the member's frames (#/mob_addressing/row_key/door).
frame.stream: GET /console/timeline/stream is one stream over the host's one frame log. With mobs=* it serves the frames of every mob the caller may address that is loaded, each frame judged for the caller in the frame's own mob; a mob that is not loaded has no frame on it, and a client that opens such a mob reads that mob's timeline, or a member's, from no cursor (meta/console/query_timeline with mob_id). Without mobs it serves the launch mob's frames.
frame.cursor: One cursor per connection: the host log's console:<seq>, opaque to the client and valid whatever the set of mobs is. A reconnect resumes by Last-Event-ID. The cursor is opaque: a client compares it and resumes with it, and reads nothing from the distance between two values. A client keeps no cursor per mob; it repairs a gap per open conversation with meta/console/query_timeline naming mob_id and identity.
frame.end: The stream has no end frame for a mob. When a mob is no longer listed to the caller its frames stop, and the mob leaves the list at the next read of the experience.

compatibility.contract_version: tolerant: contract_version is informative. No client of this contract compares it, and a client must not refuse a gateway for its value; a client reads what a gateway serves from meta/capabilities.
compatibility.older_client_newer_gateway: A client of contract v0.5.0 sends no mob_id and no mobs: it is served the launch mob as before and no member row or frame of another hosted mob; a member row and a topology node carry three members it does not read (#/mob_addressing/row_key/row_members). It reads a state word it does not know as unknown. The same holds for the lists of the host (approvals, questions, attention, audit): a request without mobs is served no entry of another mob's member, so such a client never reads another mob's member as the launch mob's member of the same name. A request made with no origin is no member's entry: meta/gating/pending and meta/gating/audit serve it to such a client where its caller may address the mob it was made for, as a request of the mob that stands under that mob's id (#/mob_addressing/mobs_selector/host_lists). Such a client meets the kind member_mob_id_required (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id/refusals) only where it names by one string a spelling two members of one door share (#/mob_addressing/row_key/shared_spelling) and is answered for both; it reads a refusal of invalid params. The kind a gateway of contract v0.5.0 answers for more than one member of one mob under one name is answered unchanged (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id/refusals/earlier_kind).
compatibility.newer_client_older_gateway: A client of this contract sends mob_id and mobs only when meta/capabilities lists mob_addressing; without it the client is the one-mob Console of contract v0.5.0.

opening.rule: There is no load word on the wire. An ordinary request that names mob_id loads a mob that is not loaded, and requests for one mob share one load. A console opens a mob a person chose with meta/status naming it, then reads the experience again.
opening.who: Any caller who may address the mob (#/mob_addressing/mob_id/judged): the method has no action gate of its own. A caller who may not address it is answered #/mob_addressing/mob_id/refusal and nothing is loaded.
opening.automatic: A client sends no request of its own accord that names a mob listed dormant or unavailable: a periodic read, a gap repair or a read on a frame skips it. Only a person's act names it.

members.note: How a request names a member of a mob, method by method.
members.member_params: A method that names a member of a mob lists, in member_params, the members of its params that name one (a dotted path; * stands for every entry). On a request of a method of scope one_mob to a hosted mob's door (#/mob_addressing/row_key/door) each of them carries the member's name as that door knows it, and the request carries that door's mob_id. The gateway's member field table reads the same words; where it accepts more than one spelling of a subject, the document names the one a client sends.
members.no_member: A method of scope one_mob without member_params names no member and takes mob_id alone: a list, a read by an id of its own, or a change of the mob. A client that acts for a member's row sends such a request to that row's door.
members.new_member: meta/fork_member names its source in source_member_id and the member it creates in agent_identity; meta/identity/create names the agents it creates in agents.*.name. A created name is a name of the door's own mob.
members.host_methods: A method of the host takes no mob as a selector. The one method of the host that names a member is meta/access/preview: its identity is the member's row key (host_member_param), and the preview is judged in that member's own mob. A row key the launch mob's door knows whole (the name of a member of the launch mob, or of a member of a mob nested under it) names that member, also when its first part is the id of another hosted mob. A row key that names no listed member is judged as a name no member has.
members.not_served_for_another_mob: In this version a member's own stream (GET /console/identity/{identity}/stream, and GET /console/timeline/stream or GET /console/timeline with mob_id) and the three /console/mcp-apps/* routes are launch_mob_only: a request on one of them that names another mob is answered #/mob_addressing/mob_id/refusal. The frames of a member of another mob are read from the one stream with mobs=* and from meta/console/query_timeline naming mob_id and identity.
members.answers: Every member the answer of a method served for one mob names, in any field, is an agent of that mob's door: it is named as that mob's door knows it and is read under the same rule as the member the request names. A reader turns it into a row key with the frame rule (#/mob_addressing/frame) and the request's mob.

limits.note: Stated limits of this contract version. Where a limit is a door that serves the launch mob only, a request on it that names another mob is answered the one refusal for every caller. The routes (#/mob_addressing/limits/routes) and the send (#/mob_addressing/limits/send) say which of their requests are served for the mob a request names, and how each of the others is answered. Lifting one is an addition.
limits.routes: Of the twelve console routes, POST /console/send and POST /console/send/recover serve the mob a request names (#/mob_addressing/limits/send). The other ten are launch_mob_only for mob_id, GET /console/gating/stream among them. Another mob is reached through the request doors (methods of scope one_mob with mob_id), the two send routes and the reads that take mobs=*.
limits.send: A send and its recovery (meta/console/send, meta/console/recover_send and the two send routes) are served for the mob a request names, for a caller the checks of a send admit in that mob: the caller may address the mob, may know of the member and holds agent.send on it there. For a member of a mob other than the launch mob six things are not served, and one is held. (1) A governed send and its recovery, on a gateway whose Console sends can be governed, are answered the typed refusal of a mob id with the member hosted: true (-32602 foreign_mob_target with data.hosted on the request door; 404 foreign_mob_target with hosted on a route). The kind is the one of a mob the gateway does not serve to the caller: a client tells the two apart by the member hosted, never by the kind or the words, and it is answered only to a caller who may address the mob. (2) A send on the door of requests with uploads (POST /console/rpc/multipart), with uploads or without, is answered the one refusal of a mob id, for every caller. (3) A member named by a runtime member id is answered an unknown identity: such a member is named by its identity. (4) A member of a mob nested under that mob, named with member_mob_id, is answered an unknown identity. (5) A schedule's fire reaches the launch mob's agents alone. (6) On a gateway that composes no identity plane, a mob without an identity runtime has no member a send reaches: the send answers an unknown identity. Held: while a mob's identity plane is not attached yet, a send and its recovery are answered the part that is not available (-32004 on the request door, after the checks of the caller; 503 unavailable on a route, for a caller who may address the mob), and the client asks again.
limits.member_stream: A member's own stream and the timeline route with mob_id are not served for a member of another mob: its frames come from the one stream with mobs=* and from meta/console/query_timeline.
limits.mcp_apps: The three /console/mcp-apps/* routes serve the launch mob's members only: an interactive view of another mob's member is not loaded.
limits.voice: The meta/console/voice/* methods and the voice channel methods serve the launch mob's members only.
limits.gating_stream: GET /console/gating/stream is launch mob only in this version and takes no selector: of the entries members made it signals a change only for an entry of the launch mob's members, and nothing for an entry of another mob's member. A request made with no origin is no member's entry: its change is signalled to the callers meta/gating/audit serves that request's rows to.
limits.methods: The request doors serve a mob other than the launch mob on the methods of scope one_mob and on no other method of this contract. They serve further methods that this contract does not list, some of them for the mob a request names. Every other method of this contract that is not the host's is launch_mob_only in this version (#/mob_addressing/scopes/launch_mob_only_methods/of_this_contract lists them): a request on it that names another mob is answered the one refusal for every caller. A method leaves the list when the door serves it per mob, which is an addition.
limits.frames_shared_spelling: A frame carries the one string and its door, and neither member_mob_id nor member_name. Where two members of one door spell one key (#/mob_addressing/row_key/shared_spelling), a frame does not say which of the two it is of. The same holds for a member an entry of a list of the host names by the frame's pair.
limits.send_retry: A send that is tried again, with the same content, by one string with the same idempotency key, after that string came to name the other member of a shared spelling (#/mob_addressing/row_key/shared_spelling), is answered the first send's acceptance: it is not sent again and does not reach the other member. The same key with other content is refused as an idempotency conflict, as for any send. The limit is the send's, and is stated with it.
limits.shared_spelling_rows: Where two members of one door spell one key (#/mob_addressing/row_key/shared_spelling), a console that lists the members of nested mobs lists neither of them in agent_sidebar.live_snapshot.agents[] in this version, and neither has a topology node: a node is built for a member row. Another member's row can still name the string (wired_to), which is then a name of no row and no node. meta/console/list_identities lists each of the two to a caller it answers for that member, and each entry names its member by the three values of its row (#/mob_addressing/member_mob_id/answer): the listing is the source of member_mob_id and member_name for a pair. Each of the two is addressed by member_mob_id and its bare name on the methods that take it. Listing both rows is an addition.
limits.member_actions: A member row of a mob other than the launch mob (with mobs=*) offers a lifecycle action only where the request doors serve the action's method for the mob a request names: each of the row's affordances can_retire (meta/retire), can_respawn (meta/respawn), can_reset (meta/reset), can_stop_run (meta/stop_member_run) and can_fork_side_chat (meta/fork_member) reads false where its method is not served per mob. In this version the stop of a run is served per mob and a retirement, a respawn, a reset and a side-chat fork are not: such a row offers the stop and none of the four. A request for one of them that names that mob is still answered the one refusal; nothing acts on another mob. A row of the launch mob reads as before.

member_mob_id.name: member_mob_id
member_mob_id.value: The id of the mob the member sits in, as the member's row states it in member_mob_id.
member_mob_id.placement: A top-level member of the request's params on POST /console/rpc, on the methods that take it. No route takes it.
member_mob_id.rule: A request that carries member_mob_id names the member of exactly that mob by exactly the name its member word carries: the bare name, never parsed. The mob is the request's own mob (the launch mob's id on the launch mob's door) or a mob listed below it. Absent or null: the member word alone names the member, as before.

methods.rule: The gateway's door holds the closed list of the methods that take it: these eight, and no other. Every other method refuses it (member_mob_id_not_accepted).

outside_this_contract.note: They take it on the gateway's door and are no methods of this contract: it has no entry for them.

roster_reads.rule: They read the roster of the mob the request is served for: member_mob_id may name that mob alone. Another mob is refused with -32602 and no kind.

methods.vocabulary: closed: a method joins the list by an addition to this contract.

member_mob_id.unknown: A member_mob_id that names no mob listed at or below the request's mob, or a name that mob does not have, is answered as a member the request's mob does not have.

member_mob_id_required.rule: On a method that takes member_mob_id and reads the name from identity, a request named by one string a spelling shared by two members the method would answer the caller for (#/mob_addressing/row_key/shared_spelling). data.identity is the one string the request named; the answer lists no member.

member_mob_id_not_accepted.rule: A request carried member_mob_id on a method that does not take it. It is refused, never ignored. data.method names the method. Every method refuses it on a console that serves no runtime of its own, and so does every request with uploads (POST /console/rpc/multipart).

refusals.vocabulary: closed: these two kinds are the refusals of a member's naming, and a third would be a breaking change. A client recognises them by data.kind, never by the message.

success.note: The schedule as meta/schedule/list answers it. Each due time is sent as a console send by the recorded sender, judged when it fires. The Console first admits the sender as it admits a live request by it: an anonymous sender only while the Console requires no sign-in; a principal only under the issuer the Console trusts then, past its provider policy and allowlist where sign-in is required, and past its session fence (Console sessions revoked after the schedule was defined refuse it, for every signed-in principal, a service identity included). Then it sends exactly as /console/send does once its caller is admitted: the candidate-launch refusal, a writable console, agent.send for the sender under the access policy then, an addressable agent whose input is not governed, and the identity-first send or the member lane. A refused or failed send fails that occurrence (delivery_failed) and the schedule keeps its later times; an agent the console no longer knows (a deleted identity, or a member without one that was retired) fails its sends the same way, and the schedule stays until it is deleted, while an identity released with meta/retire is materialized by the send, as by any console send. A send is deduplicated under its occurrence's delivery key in the sender's send scope, as a live send by the sender is, so a redelivered occurrence is sent once while the console's dedupe store holds the key (an in-memory store forgets it on restart); a send whose admission the Console could not observe (a timeout) is recorded failed although it may have been admitted.
